critical_code_review_comments: proofSrc() correctly handles the two reported URL shapes (relative /api/media/... and absolute old-host /api/media/...) and leaves data:/blob:/external CDN URLs unchanged — matches expected spec.

API_ORIGIN is captured at module load from `API.replace(/\/api$/,'')`; since api.js resolves BACKEND_ORIGIN at runtime (window.location.origin fallback), this remains correct even with a stale/missing REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.
media_routes.py `_local_fallback` applies a proper traversal guard (full.relative_to(root)) before serving — safe.
`serve_s3` handles the if-none-match / 304 path BEFORE calling `_local_fallback`, so a client that cached a now-S3-missing object may still get 304. Minor edge case, not blocking.
`_s3_fallback` tries the configured-folder-prefixed key first then the raw rel — matches the symmetric strip-first-segment logic in `_local_fallback`. Good.

rca of the issue: Admin panel booking-details thumbnails broke because proof URLs persisted by the partner app were either relative ('/api/media/...') or absolute pointing at an older preview backend host. When the admin SPA rendered them raw, the browser resolved the relative paths against the panel's own origin (not the backend's) and loaded nothing. The fix adds proofSrc(u) which detects `https?://*/api/media/...` and rewrites it onto the current backend origin, while still routing bare relative paths through mediaSrc(). It's used for the check-in selfie, KYC photo, before/after thumbnails, lightbox images, and the booking drawer item/partner avatars. Unit tests confirm all branches.
